paths.description: Public signed-out landing, representing the only reachable same-origin archetype; inspected for purpose, accessibility, preferences, responsive layout, security, performance and no-JS rendering.
Authenticated timeline, search/filter, deletion, account, error/recovery and repeated-interaction journeys; selected because these are the service core and highest-risk surfaces.

findings.summary: The signed-out page does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the default capture; the DOM reports white surfaces and color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, control, and illustration colors, with a stable light fallback.

findings.summary: Mobile lab LCP is outside the good range on a very small signed-out page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured lab LCP at 2.7 s, just outside the good <=2.5 s range, while CLS was 0 and TBT 24 ms. The separate raw-CDP trace measured LCP 1.18 s and 0 ms blocking, showing run variance but not clearing the slower mobile-style lab result.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP illustration with fetchpriority="high", reduce critical script/font competition, and retest under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavier and less prioritized than the signed-out surface requires.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 505,713 transferred bytes, including 299,897 bytes of script and 127,775 bytes of fonts. Lighthouse found the LCP image lacked fetchpriority="high", font-display could save about 70 ms, and one cache lifetime could save about 32 KiB.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image, use non-blocking font-display with metric-compatible fallbacks, and lengthen immutable static-asset caching where safe.

findings.summary: The signed-out page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 159 KiB of unused JavaScript across four bundles and 13 KiB of unused CSS; HAR shows seven scripts for a mostly static sign-in prompt.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the signed-out route from account and feedback features, conditionally load nonessential modules, and remove unused signed-out CSS.

findings.summary: The inline “Learn more” link is distinguishable only by a low-contrast color difference.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports only 1.23:1 contrast between the #2962ff link and surrounding #5f6368 text, below the 3:1 non-color distinction requirement, with no underline.
findings.suggestedFix: Underline inline links by default and ensure a non-color affordance plus sufficient contrast in every preference mode.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly prevents mobile zoom.
findings.evidence: The live DOM contains maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails the meta-viewport audit. This blocks a key low-vision adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no. Keep width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and verify reflow at 200% and 400%.

findings.summary: The main page title starts at h2 and there is no h1/main landmark.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found one H2 (“Welcome to My Activity”), no H1, a banner and footer, but no main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary content in <main> and promote the page title to a single descriptive <h1>.

findings.summary: The public signed-out landing page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM and discoverability primitive both report no meta description, although the title is descriptive and raw HTML coverage is 100%.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique meta description explaining that users can sign in to review and manage Google activity.

findings.summary: The signed-out response has avoidable policy gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows CSP includes unsafe-eval in one policy and no Referrer-Policy header. HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN, Trusted Types enforcement, and Permissions-Policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval from the applicable script policy if compatibility permits and send an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: The public sign-in prompt performs disproportionate background and unused work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 22 requests and 505,713 transferred bytes for a small static prompt, while Lighthouse estimated 159 KiB unused JavaScript and 13 KiB unused CSS. Twenty requests and 447,510 bytes came from other Google origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a lean signed-out bundle and defer feedback, app-menu, analytics/logging, and account-only modules until requested or authenticated.
